question: What is a major risk when hospital waste isn't disposed of properly in the community?
explanation: You've got this! Improperly managed medical waste carries germs that can leak into our environment and make the public sick. Always good to keep safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why is you, the bedside nurse, so important in hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses write all national environmental health laws
options.B: Nurses are solely responsible for incinerator operations
options.C: Nurses supervise the daily clinical actions at the point of generation
options.D: Nurses purchase all hospital disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because you provide direct patient care every day, you control how waste is sorted and handled right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which of these everyday ward items belongs to the general waste category?

options.A: Food wrappers from the ward kitchen

explanation: That's correct! General waste is non-hazardous and similar to ordinary household rubbish, like paper and food packaging. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: How do we classify used surgical blades and needles in the hospital?
explanation: Great job! Any tool that can cut or puncture the skin, like needles and blades, is known specifically as a sharp. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: How does rotating your stock help reduce waste on the ward?

options.A: It increases the daily consumption of PPE
options.B: It speeds up the sorting of infectious linen
options.C: It ensures needles are sterilized twice
options.D: It prevents medications from expiring on the shelf

explanation: Exactly! Using older drugs first ensures they get used before their expiry date, stopping them from turning into wasted medicine. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: A nurse prepares an exact dose of an injectable drug and saves the remainder carefully. What good nursing practice does this show?

options.C: A direct breach of universal safety laws
options.D: Waste reduction and efficient resource use

explanation: Well done! Careful dosing avoids unnecessary surplus that would otherwise end up being thrown away. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: At what point should healthcare waste be sorted or segregated?

options.A: Once a week by the sanitation crew
options.B: Immediately at the point of origin
options.C: After transport to the incinerator site
options.D: During the final sorting at the dumpsite

explanation: Spot on! We always sort waste right where it is generated so dangerous items don't mix with regular rubbish. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: What color and type of container is standard for collecting used sharps in the ward?
explanation: You got it! Sharps need hard, puncture-proof containers—usually yellow with biohazard signs—to keep everyone safe from needle sticks. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why should you never use your hands to press down or compress trash in a waste bag?

options.A: It causes the plastic bag to dissolve quickly
options.B: Hidden needles can puncture the skin and cause injury
options.C: It slows down the overall cleaning schedule
options.D: It changes the color code of the plastic bag

explanation: That's right! Pressing down on bags can hide stray needles that might easily pierce the plastic and injure you. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: How full should a waste bag be before you tie it up and remove it from the ward?
explanation: Brilliant! We tie and remove bags at three-quarters full so there's enough room to close them safely without tearing or spilling. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the main job of an autoclave in medical waste processing?

options.A: Burning plastic waste into black ash
options.B: Using steam under pressure to sterilize items
options.D: Crushing glass ampoules into fine powder

explanation: Spot on! Autoclaves use hot steam under pressure to kill germs on equipment, making them safe to handle or throw away. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why do we use incineration for body tissues and pathological waste?

options.A: It is the cheapest method available for liquid chemicals
options.B: It allows the tissues to be reused in laboratory practicals
options.C: High temperatures completely destroy biological tissue and reduce infection risks
options.D: It converts body parts into recyclable plastic materials

explanation: That's correct! Extreme heat completely destroys anatomical parts safely, keeping the environment and public healthy. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: Oh no! A nurse gets a needle stick injury while dealing with a full sharps box. What is the very first thing she should do?

options.A: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.B: Complete an incident report form before washing the wound
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site hard to force out old blood
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow immediately

explanation: You've got it! Immediate washing with soap and running water helps wash away germs right away before you report the incident. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which of these items is NOT safe or recommended for hospital waste handlers to wear?
explanation: Spot on! Open shoes leave feet exposed to falling sharps, chemical spills, and heavy equipment. Always wear closed shoes on duty! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)
